brief.situation: You are the network technician at Larkspur Insurance, a fictional company. Last night a contractor replaced ACC-SW2, the floor 2 access switch, loading its configuration from a template. At 08:30 floor 2's PCs cannot reach anything; floor 2's IP phones work, and floor 1 is fine. The floor 2 payroll team must submit by 09:15. Find the fault and fix it without breaking anything else.
handover: VLAN 20 is staff PCs (10.20.20.0/24), VLAN 30 voice, VLAN 99 management (you reach ACC-SW2 over SSH on VLAN 99). CORE1 routes the VLANs and relays DHCP to DHCP1.
ACC-SW2's uplink Gi1/0/48 is an 802.1Q trunk to CORE1 Gi1/0/2. Reaching ACC-SW2's console means walking to the floor 2 closet.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, device or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command or change takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. The payroll cutoff is 09:15, 45 minutes after the first report.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what the 169.254 addresses told you, where the fault was and how you proved it, and why your change could not break anything else.

parts.label: Symptom
parts.criteria: Reads 169.254.x.x with no gateway as a link-local address a host takes when no DHCP server answers, and uses the working phones and floor 1 to narrow it to VLAN 20 on floor 2.
parts.modelAnswer: 169.254 with no gateway means the PCs got no DHCP answer and gave themselves link-local addresses. Phones on the same ports and all of floor 1 worked, so DHCP itself and the access ports were fine; only VLAN 20 from floor 2 was cut off.

parts.label: Fault and proof
parts.criteria: Finds VLAN 20 missing from the allowed list of ACC-SW2's uplink trunk with show interfaces trunk (and the DHCP scope not exhausted).
parts.modelAnswer: show interfaces trunk on ACC-SW2 listed 30,99 as allowed on Gi1/0/48; the template left out 20. The DHCP scope had 141 free addresses, so it was not exhaustion.

parts.label: Safe change
parts.criteria: Uses switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20 (or the full list), explains that a bare list replaces the allowed VLANs and would drop voice and management, saves the configuration and verifies with a renew.
parts.modelAnswer: I used allowed vlan add 20, because a bare 'allowed vlan 20' replaces the list and would have dropped voice VLAN 30 and my own management VLAN 99. Then I saved it and renewed a floor 2 PC, which got 10.20.20.57 and its gateway.

expertPath.text: ipconfig on a floor 2 PC: 169.254, no gateway, so no DHCP answer. Phones and floor 1 work, and the VLAN 20 scope has free addresses.
On ACC-SW2, show vlan brief is right; show interfaces trunk lists 30,99 on Gi1/0/48; CORE1's side allows everything.
switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20, copy running-config startup-config, ipconfig /renew on PC-F2-14.
Record the template's allowed list as the cause, and fix the template.

fixed.headline: Good: fixed at the trunk
fixed.body: You read 169.254 as no DHCP answer, followed it to the uplink's allowed list and added VLAN 20 without touching the others, then saved and verified.

fixedGaps.headline: Fixed, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: Floor 2 works. The criteria show what it cost: time, a change before the evidence, an unsaved fix or a reload.

voiceDropped.headline: The fix broke voice
voiceDropped.body: switchport trunk allowed vlan with a bare list replaces the list; add appends. Replacing it took voice and your own management VLAN off the uplink.

reloadedUnsaved.headline: Reloaded without saving
reloadedUnsaved.body: A reload boots the startup configuration. Save first, and do not reload a working access switch in business hours.

payrollMissed.headline: The outage reached payroll
payrollMissed.body: Floor 1 and the phones working said DHCP was fine. The uplink trunk's allowed list was one show command away.

stillDown.headline: Closed too soon
stillDown.body: Floor 2's PCs still had link-local addresses. Fix, then renew a PC before you close.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: 169.254 addresses with no gateway mean no DHCP answer. Phones on the same ports and floor 1 working rule out the DHCP server and the access ports; the scope has free addresses, so it is not exhaustion. show interfaces trunk on ACC-SW2 shows VLAN 20 missing from Gi1/0/48's allowed list. Add it with switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20 (a bare list replaces the list and would drop voice and management), save with copy running-config startup-config, and verify with ipconfig /renew on a floor 2 PC.
